articles.title: Comet Terrace
articles.summary: Bright orange and cream diagonal shards fanning out like a shattered sunburst, heavy sparkle, satin metal finish. Reads as a warm copper and cream curved-bar pattern with a dark corner zone, like woven copper wire or a hand fan; high contrast between zones.
articles.what: Shattered ring terraces igniting sector by sector under a sweeping radar arm Up close: Curved rows of glossy tube segments, like bundled copper pipes, arcing across the panel. Each rod is 15-20 px thick, shaded round with a bright highlight stripe, in copper-orange and cream-gold, some segments near-black brown. Large circular sector edges cut it into zones: dark brown, cream, then. From a distance: Reads as a warm copper and cream curved-bar pattern with a dark corner zone, like woven copper wire or a hand fan; high contrast between zones. Measured spec (average): metal 179, roughness 83, coat 202. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: hood, roof, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Comet Terrace" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: the arcs flow across wide panels and the sector edges read as feature lines
Avoid small trim: the rods are too big there
Hard: strong bright and dark rods cut numbers, so use a solid plate in black or cream with a border.
Large soft shapes (fades, blocks): the rods are medium, so big shapes sit above
Pairs well with: black, cream, dark brown, chrome.
pitfalls: Not smooth copper: the render is round rods with dark gaps and zones
Not carbon fibre: the segments are rounded copper tubes in arcs, no twill
Avoid: numbers over the shard pattern, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 179 (true metallic), roughness 83 (satin gloss), clearcoat 202 (almost no clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers over the shard pattern, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large soft shapes (fades, blocks): the rods are medium, so big shapes sit above; bold stripes and number plates: needed because it is busy
Patterns to avoid: other stripe, weave or wave patterns: curved lines collide; glitter and flake: sparkle is already at maximum
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat on a number block: smooth patch; none elsewhere: strong metal variation is built in
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
